grades.quote: At this point, please read kernel/syscall.c, sys_write() in kernel/sysfile.c, and copyout(), copyin(), and copyinstr() in kernel/vm.c.
grades.reason: Covers how system call arguments and numbers reach the kernel through registers and the trapframe. It only points the reader to copyin, copyout and copyinstr in kernel/vm.c. It doesn't explain how a string is safely copied from user memory.

grades.quote: The functions copyin and copyinstr walk the user page table in software.
grades.reason: An exercise item that states copyin and copyinstr walk the user page table in software to copy system call arguments into the kernel. That is a small piece of the mechanism, but the passage doesn't describe the safe string copy itself.
Security-model background. It notes that user code may pass clever values to system calls, but it says nothing about how xv6 copies argument strings from user memory.
Index page. It lists copyinstr and copyout with page numbers and gives no explanation of how they work.
